newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan foreign minister visits Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan foreign minister visits Belgium.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister is visiting Belgium on an unofficial diplomatic mission, the mass-circulation United Daily News reported on Sunday.

The newspaper said Foreign Minister John Chang flew to Brussels on Saturday following a visit to South Africa, where he tried to reverse Pretoria's November 27 decision to switch diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei.
Media reports had suggested Chang was likely to visit African countries to seek new diplomatic ties after his stay in Brussels, but Chang denied this.
"This (visit) has nothing to do with any African countries," Chang told state television in an interview in Brussels.
Chang said his visit to Belgium was mainly private.
"(I) simply came to visit some friends here," he said.
Reuters checked with the European Commission and Belgium foreign ministry and they said no meetings scheduled with Chang.

"I can clearly say (the visit) is not related to discussing forging diplomatic ties with certain countries," Chang told the United Daily News in a telephone interview. "But considering my position, you can say it's related to diplomatic interests."
"There will be no official visit...," he said.
Chang said he would return to Taipei on Tuesday or Wednesday. He was originally scheduled to return on Sunday.
Vice-foreign minister Cheng Chien-jen said on Saturday Chang had left South Africa and was visiting other countries, but he declined to give more details.
South African President Nelson Mandela announced last month that Pretoria, the biggest of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies, would switch ties to Beijing in 1997.
Communist China regards Taiwan as a renegade province following a civil war which divided them in 1949.
Chang met Mandela on Wednesday but the South African president said he would stick by his "agonising decision" to sever ties with Taiwan.
Chang said on Thursday that Taipei would recall its ambassador to South Africa and immediately suspend all aid projects and treaties in protest at Pretoria's decision.
